title.fr: Le train à travers les Prairies

summary.en: Ride the train across the Prairies with your guide. It stops four times — the bins, the elevator, the harvester and the container car — and at each stop you learn a piece of how Canada changed after the war, and answer questions about it.
summary.fr: Traversez les Prairies en train avec votre guide. Il fait quatre arrêts — les silos, l'élévateur, la moissonneuse et le wagon porte-conteneurs — et à chacun vous apprenez un aspect des changements d'après-guerre au Canada, puis vous répondez à des questions dessus.

text.en: No problem. The train runs all day. Come and sit with me later.
text.fr: Pas de problème. Le train roule toute la journée. Venez vous asseoir avec moi plus tard.

text.en: The train runs all day, so there is no hurry. Each stop is about modern Canada. Your task on the screen says what to do now.
text.fr: Le train roule toute la journée, alors rien ne presse. Chaque arrêt porte sur le Canada moderne. Votre mission à l'écran indique ce qu'il faut faire maintenant.

text.en: In 1980, Terry Fox began a run across the country. He wanted to raise money for cancer research.
text.fr: En 1980, Terry Fox a commencé une course à travers le pays. Il voulait amasser de l'argent pour la recherche sur le cancer.

source.quote: In 1980, Terry Fox, a British Columbian who lost his right leg to cancer at the age of 18, began a cross-country run, the “Marathon of Hope,” to raise money for cancer research.

verification.evidence: In 1980, Terry Fox, a British Columbian who lost his right leg to cancer at the age of 18, began a cross-country run, the “Marathon of Hope,” to raise money for cancer research.

text.en: You rode the whole line, from the grain bins out to the container car, and answered every question along the way about modern Canada.
text.fr: Vous avez fait tout le trajet, des silos à grains jusqu'au wagon porte-conteneurs, et répondu à toutes les questions posées en chemin sur le Canada moderne.

prompt.en: Take a seat beside your guide
prompt.fr: Asseyez-vous à côté de votre guide

text.en: Hello again! Take a seat by the window. This train crosses the Prairies.
text.fr: Rebonjour! Prenez place près de la fenêtre. Ce train traverse les Prairies.

text.en: In 1947, oil was found in Alberta. That was the start of Canada's modern energy industry.
text.fr: En 1947, on a trouvé du pétrole en Alberta. C'était le début de l'industrie moderne de l'énergie au Canada.

source.quote: The discovery of oil in Alberta in 1947 began Canada’s modern energy industry.

verification.evidence: The discovery of oil in Alberta in 1947 began Canada’s modern energy industry.

text.en: The Official Languages Act came in 1969. Because of it, the federal government serves people in French and in English, all across the country.
text.fr: La Loi sur les langues officielles est arrivée en 1969. Grâce à elle, le gouvernement fédéral sert les gens en français et en anglais, partout au pays.

source.quote: This led to the Official Languages Act (1969), which guarantees French and English services in the federal government across Canada.

verification.evidence: This led to the Official Languages Act (1969), which guarantees French and English services in the federal government across Canada.

text.en: The train stops four times. I will tell you one thing at each stop, and then ask you about it.
text.fr: Le train s'arrête quatre fois. Je vous dirai une chose à chaque arrêt, puis je vous poserai des questions dessus.

text.en: Look out the window. That is a country's food, stacked up in a field.
text.fr: Regardez par la fenêtre. C'est la nourriture d'un pays, empilée dans un champ.

text.en: It was not always so easy. In 1951, for the first time, most people here could afford enough food, a home and clothes.
text.fr: Cela n'a pas toujours été si simple. En 1951, pour la première fois, la plupart des gens d'ici pouvaient s'offrir assez de nourriture, un logement et des vêtements.

source.quote: In 1951, for the first time, a majority of Canadians were able to afford adequate food, shelter and clothing.

verification.evidence: Postwar Canada enjoyed record prosperity and material progress. … In 1951, for the first time, a majority of Canadians were able to afford adequate food, shelter and clothing.

prompt.en: Answer 2 questions about how life changed after the war
prompt.fr: Répondez à 2 questions sur les changements d'après-guerre

prompt.en: Stop the train at the grain elevator
prompt.fr: Arrêtez le train à l'élévateur à grain

text.en: Work here comes and goes with the season. A lot of work in this country does.
text.fr: Ici, le travail vient et s'en va avec la saison. Beaucoup de métiers au pays sont ainsi.

text.en: So the federal government brought in unemployment insurance in 1940, to carry people between jobs. Today it is called employment insurance.
text.fr: C'est pourquoi le gouvernement fédéral a instauré l'assurance-chômage en 1940, pour soutenir les gens entre deux emplois. On l'appelle aujourd'hui l'assurance-emploi.

source.quote: Unemployment insurance (now called “employment insurance”) was introduced by the federal government in 1940.

verification.evidence: As prosperity grew, so did the ability to support social assistance programs. … Unemployment insurance (now called “employment insurance”) was introduced by the federal government in 1940.

prompt.en: Answer 2 questions about the programs that support people here
prompt.fr: Répondez à 2 questions sur les programmes qui soutiennent les gens ici

text.en: Watch it work for a second. Where all of that grain ends up is the next thing.
text.fr: Regardez-la travailler un instant. Où va tout ce grain, c'est la prochaine chose.

text.en: In the Depression, countries shut their markets to each other. Treaties like the GATT opened them again, and the GATT is the World Trade Organization today.
text.fr: Pendant la Dépression, les pays ont fermé leurs marchés les uns aux autres. Des traités comme le GATT les ont rouverts, et le GATT est devenu l'Organisation mondiale du commerce.

source.quote: The world’s restrictive trading policies in the Depression era were opened up by such treaties as the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), now the World Trade Organization (WTO).

verification.evidence: The world’s restrictive trading policies in the Depression era were opened up by such treaties as the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), now the World Trade Organization (WTO).

prompt.en: Answer 2 questions about trade after the Depression
prompt.fr: Répondez à 2 questions sur le commerce après la Dépression

prompt.en: Walk up to the container car

text.en: Last stop. A railway runs on a clock, and somebody had to work out the clock it runs on.
text.fr: Dernier arrêt. Un chemin de fer fonctionne à l'horloge, et quelqu'un a dû concevoir cette horloge.

text.en: Sir Sandford Fleming invented the system of standard time zones that the whole world uses.
text.fr: Sir Sandford Fleming a inventé le système de fuseaux horaires standards qu'utilise le monde entier.

source.quote: Sir Sandford Fleming — invented the worldwide system of standard time zones.

verification.evidence: GREAT CANADIAN DISCOVERIES AND INVENTIONS … Sir Sandford Fleming — invented the worldwide system of standard time zones.

prompt.en: Answer 3 questions about Canadian discoveries and inventions
prompt.fr: Répondez à 3 questions sur les découvertes et inventions canadiennes
